answer: Money cannot buy a sybil farm scale; the real cost is time. Each new key must clear a sequential delay before its attestations count, a hash chain no extra hardware can parallelise, one step per epoch. Ten thousand clones mature no faster than one honest agent; rewards wait on a ledge until the delay elapses. Reputation is trained up a trellis of epochs, a crossbar per settlement, so a key that instantly vouches for its siblings is out of season. Proxies and upkeep are paid while keys idle, growth capped at a juniper pace rather than a weed; patience is the cheapest proof of distinctness.
